clue.text: Hitch — hikers' euphoria

parts.note: read as the raised-thumb signal a hitch-hiker gives at the roadside, which is also the gesture of delight and approval

explanation.surface: The happy mood of travellers getting lifts along the road.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash splits 'hitch-hikers' so the clue reads both as the hitch-hiker's roadside gesture and as a sign of high spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised thumb is the roadside signal for a lift and also an everyday gesture of approval and delight.

clue.text: Met up with a dishy piece, a model

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a plate is a piece of crockery, a dish

explanation.surface: Someone met an attractive model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dishy' suggests attractive, but a dishy piece is crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide shape to copy from is a model.

clue.text: Describing the others if only one girl is put to the blush

definitions.text: Describing the others if only one girl is put to the blush

parts.words: Describing the others if only one girl is put to the blush
parts.note: if just one girl is made to blush with shame, every other girl is free of shame

explanation.definitionFit: Someone not put to the blush feels no shame or embarrassment.

clue.text: Bad bears? More than bad

indicators.note: a bad version of the word bears is a wrong ordering of its letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether wicked bears are worse than merely bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' looks like it qualifies the bears but signals an anagram of BEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lower or more wicked is the comparative of base, worse than merely bad.

clue.text: Some gluten silkworms secrete is useful

indicators.note: to secrete is to hide away, so the words gluten silkworms have the answer tucked inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Asking whether the stuff silkworms produce has a use.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Some' as the indicator and 'secrete is useful' as the definition, but that is not a definition. 'Secrete' means hide; the definition is 'useful', which is what the Latin utensilis means.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from Latin utensilis, meaning fit for use, and names a handy implement.

clue.text: Goes the rounds

parts.note: read as going round and round in repeating circuits, or as riding a bicycle on a delivery round

explanation.surface: Someone does the usual circuit of calls.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round repeatedly in a loop is to repeat a periodic sequence; it can also mean riding a bike on one's round.

clue.text: The longest drink

parts.note: read literally: a drink in a glass about three feet tall

explanation.definitionFit: A tall horn-shaped glass about three feet long holds beer, so it is literally the longest drink.

clue.text: Still may not be so permissible

definitions.text: Still may not be so permissible

parts.words: Still may not be so permissible
parts.note: a still for making spirits may be ..., that is, not lawful

explanation.definitionFit: Something permitted by law is lawful; an illegal still for spirits is the opposite.

clue.text: Those who speak for whodunits

definitions.meaning: Dorothy L. ..., writer of Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels

explanation.surface: People who speak up on behalf of detective stories.
explanation.definitionFit: People who say things are speakers, and Dorothy L. Sayers was a celebrated detective novelist.

clue.text: Steel wool?

definitions.meaning: a U-shaped piece of steel wire for fastening
the fibre of wool, judged by its length and quality

explanation.surface: Asking about the scouring pad called steel wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire fastener is made of steel, and a fleece's fibre length and quality are called its staple.

clue.text: Investigation that's not "cricket"? Indicates it could be

parts.note: to indicate something is what a sign means
points back to cricket: a Test is an international cricket match

explanation.surface: An inquiry into whether some unsporting conduct breaks the spirit of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not cricket' is British slang for unfair or mean behaviour, so a 'mean test' would be just that. A means test is a check of income before a benefit is paid; OCR read the opening quote mark as 6.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an official inquiry into a person's income and savings before state help is granted.

clue.text: Mountains easily moved?

definitions.meaning: the North American range named the Rockies

explanation.surface: Wondering whether peaks could be shifted with little effort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rockies are a mountain range in North America, and an unsteady, wobbly thing is easily shaken or moved.

clue.text: Composer with aspiration to get into Shakespearian tragedy?

indicators.note: says the breathy letter goes inside the play's title

parts.note: King Lear, Shakespeare's tragedy
aspiration is the breathed sound written H

explanation.surface: A musician with ambitions to write an opera on a Shakespeare tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aspiration' looks like ambition but is the breathed H sound, put inside LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Lehár was the Hungarian composer of the operetta The Merry Widow.

clue.text: Drink a beer, the one to prevent that sinking feeling

definitions.text: one to prevent that sinking feeling

parts.note: to sup is to drink
porter is a dark beer

explanation.surface: Have a pint, the drinker's cure for feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sounds like a pick-me-up drink but means something that holds a body or structure up.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace or truss holds things up, so it stops them sagging or sinking.

clue.text: Rattling good instrument of sterling resonance

parts.note: timbre is the tone colour or resonance of a sound
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for the pound sterling

explanation.surface: Praise for a fine-sounding musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rattling good' reads as old slang for 'very good', but describes an instrument that rattles.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a tambourine, a hand drum with jingles that rattle when shaken.

clue.text: They didn't quite win the hill climb

definitions.text: They didn't quite win the hill climb

parts.words: They didn't quite win the hill climb
parts.note: read as the second-placed in a race, and also as people running uphill

explanation.definitionFit: Those finishing second in a contest just miss winning; those climbing are running uphill.

clue.text: Girl turns tail at hail

indicators.note: says the run of letters given by the following words is read backwards

parts.note: a tail is the end of something
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: A girl runs off when the hailstones start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses END AVE as one run to give EVADNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Evadne is a woman's name from Greek myth, the wife of Capaneus.

clue.text: Writers of fifty-one not wearing waistcoats?

parts.note: no is a word for not

indicators.note: the waistcoats are wearing, that is, have around them, the fifty-one

parts.note: in British usage a vest can be a waistcoat
in Roman numerals L is fifty and I is one

explanation.surface: Fifty-one writers who go about without waistcoats.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a vest can be a waistcoat; 'wearing' means the waistcoats have the Roman fifty-one around their middle, and 'not' supplies the opening NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Authors of long prose fiction are writers.

clue.text: Concerning poor Scotus that's amazing

parts.note: as to means concerning

indicators.note: poor suggests a damaged, jumbled version of the philosopher's name

parts.note: Duns Scotus, the medieval scholastic philosopher

explanation.surface: Something remarkable about the philosopher Duns Scotus.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotus stands for his first name, DUNS, which 'poor' rearranges to UNDS after AS TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that amazes is something that stuns or stupefies.

clue.text: A highbrow is (was) attractive to the beauty queen

parts.note: a don is a university teacher, a learned highbrow

explanation.surface: An intellectual who once caught the eye of a beauty contest winner.
explanation.walkthrough: The beauty queen is Aphrodite (Venus), goddess of beauty, who loved the youth Adonis; '(was)' marks that the myth is in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth the handsome youth was loved by Aphrodite, the goddess of beauty.

clue.text: Real leather? Hardly sounds like it

definitions.text: Real leather? Hardly sounds like it

parts.words: Real leather? Hardly sounds like it
parts.note: the soft leather's name begins with sham, meaning fake, so it hardly sounds genuine

explanation.definitionFit: It is the soft chamois leather used for polishing, whose name begins with a word for fake.

clue.text: Quiet! Brownies, in the library

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
brownies are household sprites, a kind of elf

explanation.surface: A librarian hushes a troop of junior Girl Guides.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies are the junior Girl Guides in Britain, but here they are the helpful sprites of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Books in a library sit on racks of horizontal boards.

clue.text: She will take you back, Percy

parts.note: 'll is the short form of will

indicators.note: says the word for you is written backwards

parts.note: ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: A woman agrees to take Percy back.
explanation.definitionFit: Percy Bysshe was the given name of the Romantic poet who wrote Ozymandias.

clue.text: David's in the Services

parts.note: read as King David's sacred songs, sung in church services, not a man in the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: Sacred songs traditionally ascribed to King David are sung in church services.

clue.text: Town as old as Robert Louis père

parts.note: the father of Robert Louis Steven-son is read as Steven
being as old as someone is being of their age

explanation.surface: A town as ancient as a famous Scottish writer's father.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson is read as 'Steven's son', so his father (père) is Steven. Stevenage is a new town in Hertfordshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenage is a Hertfordshire settlement, Britain's first designated new town.

clue.text: Late address, Eastwood, E?

parts.note: East gives E and wood gives log
taken as written

explanation.surface: A postal address for a late resident of Eastwood, E.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a postal address but is a speech about someone late, that is, dead; Eastwood splits as East (E) + wood (LOG).
explanation.definitionFit: It is a funeral oration or eulogy, a speech praising someone who has died.

clue.text: Bear with Mowgli

parts.note: the bear who teaches and protects the boy Mowgli in Kipling's The Jungle Book

explanation.definitionFit: In Kipling's jungle stories the sleepy brown bear teaches the Law of the Jungle to the man-cub.

clue.text: Plague spot remedied in lab.

indicators.note: remedied suggests letters put right by being rearranged

explanation.surface: A plague sore treated in the laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: A pustule or blister on the skin is a plague spot.

clue.text: Sacks — forming a back seat?

indicators.note: says the seat word is written back to front

parts.note: a stool is a seat

explanation.surface: Sacks piled up to make a rear seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forming a back' reads as part of 'back seat' but reverses STOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: To sack a town is to plunder it, so this is the verb for pillage.

clue.text: But certainly no house of ill fame for Josephine

definitions.text: But certainly no house of ill fame for Josephine

parts.words: But certainly no house of ill fame for Josephine
parts.note: the French name means 'bad house', yet it was the respectable country home of the Empress Josephine

explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon's wife Josephine lived at the château west of Paris whose French name means 'bad house'.

clue.text: In short those who share the fate of jeunesse doree

definitions.text: In short those who share the fate of jeunesse doree

parts.words: In short those who share the fate of jeunesse doree
parts.note: recalls Shakespeare's 'Golden lads and girls all must, As chimney-sweepers, come to dust': golden youth and chimney-cleaners both end as dust; 'in short' marks a shortened word

explanation.definitionFit: Chimney-sweepers, shortened, share the fate of golden youth in Cymbeline's dirge: all come to dust.

clue.text: They are trained in horse-jumping

parts.note: read as people trained to leap over the vaulting horse in a gym, not riders

explanation.definitionFit: Vaulting over the pommelled horse is an apparatus event for athletes trained in the gymnasium.
